title: 机器狗背70公斤爬泰山，累不累？
title_en: A Robot Dog Hauled 70 kg Up Mount Tai. Is It Tired?

segments.zh: 一只机器狗，背着七十公斤，
segments.en: A robot dog carried seventy kilograms
up Mount Tai.
How heavy is seventy kilograms?

segments.zh: 差不多背着一个成年人。
segments.en: About one grown-up on its back.

segments.zh: 这是11月2日开赛的泰山机器人登山赛，
segments.en: This was the Mount Tai robot climbing contest that opened November second,
and it won the load race.

segments.zh: 据报道，它的额定负重只有五十公斤，
segments.en: Reportedly its rated load is only fifty kilograms.
On this stretch it was overloaded.
Today's brain teaser:

segments.zh: 机器狗背七十公斤爬泰山，到底累不累？
segments.en: does a robot dog get tired hauling seventy kilos up Mount Tai?
Meet our hero, Lingling,
a four-legged robot dog.
It has no muscles.
Each leg has a few motors.
Climbing is really just
lifting stuff higher.

segments.zh: 每一级台阶，就像把箱子
segments.en: Every step is like lifting a box
onto the next shelf.
The physics rule:

segments.zh: 做的功 = 重量 × 高度。
segments.en: work equals weight times height.

segments.zh: 估算一下：七十公斤抬高一米，
segments.en: Rough estimate: lifting seventy kilos one meter
takes about seven hundred joules.
One step is fifteen centimeters or so.
That is over one hundred joules per step.
If it hauled all the way to the summit,
that is over a thousand meters up, roughly.
Seventy kilos up a thousand meters
works out to nearly a million joules.
How much is a million joules?

segments.zh: 大约四块大号充电宝的电。
segments.en: About four big power banks.

segments.zh: 可电机会发热，腿还要找平衡，
segments.en: But motors heat up and legs keep balancing,

segments.zh: 实际耗的电得多好几倍，这是推测。
segments.en: so the real bill is several times more. That's our guess.
Twist one: fast or slow,
the work stays exactly the same.
Rush up in one go,

segments.zh: 和歇十次再上去，一样多。
segments.en: or rest ten times, it is the same amount.

segments.zh: 走得快，只是每秒花得多，
segments.en: Going fast only spends more per second.
That is called power.
Like paying for something:

segments.zh: 总价一样，只是一次付还是分期付。
segments.en: same price, all at once or in installments.
So why four legs
and not two?
Think of a stool:

segments.zh: 三条腿的凳子，怎么放都不晃。
segments.en: a three-legged stool never wobbles.
When the robot dog lifts one leg,
three are still holding it up.

segments.zh: 两条腿的人形机器人抬一条腿，
segments.en: When a two-legged humanoid lifts one leg,

segments.zh: 只剩一个点，得一直找平衡。
segments.en: only one point is left, so it must keep balancing.
So for heavy loads,
four legs have a built-in edge.
What about humanoids?

segments.zh: 据报道，它们也在乱台阶上比了竞速。
segments.en: Reportedly they raced on the messy steps too.
Two legs are harder,

segments.zh: 可人走的路，全是给两条腿修的。
segments.en: but every path people walk was built for two legs.
Twist two, the strangest:
standing still also burns power.
By the physics definition,
holding still does zero work.
But the motors push to hold on.

segments.zh: 电流一直在流，全变成了热。
segments.en: Current keeps flowing, and it all turns into heat.

segments.zh: 你端着一桶水站着不动，
segments.en: Hold a bucket of water without moving,
and your arm still gets sore.
So the robot dog does not get tired,
but its motors heat up and its battery drains.
Twist three: on Mount Tai,
the hard part is not the height, it is the mess.

segments.zh: 据报道，台阶高低宽窄都不一样，
segments.en: Reportedly the steps vary in height and width,
so every step needs a new calculation.

segments.zh: 机器狗靠眼睛和腿上的感觉，
segments.en: The dog uses cameras and the feel in its legs
to feel its way, step by step.
Now the human porters of Mount Tai:

segments.zh: 据央视报道，一趟挑三四十公斤。
segments.en: according to CCTV, about thirty to forty kilos a trip.
The robot dog carried seventy,
about double on pure strength.
But porters can go all day.
The robot dog needs to find a charger.

segments.zh: 据报道，登山赛上还有人穿着助力外骨骼，
segments.en: Reportedly, one climber wore an assist exoskeleton

segments.zh: 大约一小时就上了中天门。
segments.en: and reached the halfway gate in about an hour.

segments.zh: 机器不一定要替人爬山，
segments.en: Machines don't have to climb for us.
They can help us climb.

segments.zh: 友情提示：七十公斤、五十公斤额定是据报道，
segments.en: Fine print: seventy kilos and the fifty kilo rating are as reported.

segments.zh: 七百焦、一百多焦是估算。
segments.en: Seven hundred joules and over one hundred per step are estimates.
A contest is one day's result,

segments.zh: 离天天上山干活还有距离。
segments.en: still far from hauling up the mountain every day.
So does the robot dog get tired?

segments.zh: 它不会累，只会热、只会没电。
segments.en: It never gets tired. It only gets hot and runs out of battery.

segments.zh: 泰山不是一口气爬上去的，
segments.en: Nobody climbs Mount Tai in one go.
It gets lifted, one step at a time.
